key_insight: Subtle tetragonal distortion in smaller BaTiO3 nanoparticles boosts dipole coherence, polarization, and charge retention, enabling strong lead-free piezoelectric nanogenerator performance.
engineering_relevance: By tuning particle size and covalency in BaTiO3, the study shows a practical route to higher-output self-powered devices for wearables and low-power electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Structural confirmation with XRD, Raman, and pair distribution function analysis
DFT to probe Ti–O bonding, band gap, and dipole coherence
evidence_signal: BTO-900 (~54 nm) showed ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 μJ stored energy, while BTO-1200 (~104 nm) delivered higher peak power density (~649 μW cm−2) and short-circuit current (~181 μA).
watch_item: Device performance depends on nanoparticle size, annealing, and interfacial charge trapping, so optimization may not transfer directly across fabrication conditions or encapsulation schemes.
paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
